props.gloss_en: the Sages: either way one may shutter [the window] with it
Rav Kahana: [either way means] whether tied or not tied, provided it is prepared
R' Yirmeya: let the Master say -- whether hanging or not hanging, provided it is tied
R' Yochanan: as the dispute here, so is the dispute over the dragged bolt
a dragged bolt -- one locks with it in the Temple
...but not in the country
and a placed [bolt] is forbidden here and there
R' Yehuda: the placed one [is permitted] in the Temple
R' Yehuda: and the dragged one in the country
the baraita: the dragged bolt that locks in the Temple but not in the country is any that is tied and hanging and its end reaches the ground
R' Yehuda: rather, what is forbidden in the country is any [bolt] neither tied nor hanging, which one removes and puts in a corner
Ulla: who taught the dragged bolt? It is R' Eliezer
a reed the householder set up to open and lock with: when it is tied and hanging at the doorway, one may open and lock with it

R' Yochanan: the halakha follows RSBG
all covers of vessels that have a handle may be moved on Shabbat
R' Yochanan: provided they have the status of a vessel

RSBG: he need not tie [them]
R' Yitzchak Nappacha: the halakha follows R' Eliezer

Abaye: what is your thought -- because it is taught unattributed? The dragged bolt is also unattributed
